//: Built-in agent registry, used by every project without a registry entry that replaces this file. It is the ONLY place a provider name appears in the collaboration layer: the protocol routes by role and capability, never by agent id.
//briefing: `briefing` is the agent's own instructions, returned by its whoami call. `briefing_file` is relative to this directory.
//roles: No agent here has roles or capabilities: which agent holds which role is the person's composition (machine agents.json, outside git). An agent may have every capability except the ones its program cannot have in principle (`adapter.cannot`, a fact about the vendor's program, not a decision about roles); every role those capabilities satisfy is offered, and the facts on the machine (probe.mjs) rule out the rest (ADR-0026).
//adapter: `adapter.kind` is how a message physically reaches the agent. 'manual' = it lands in the inbox and the agent reads it when its session runs. 'cli' = the layer could spawn it; `enabled:false` means it will not. `adapter.headless` (manual agents) lists the commands through which ANOTHER agent can start this one on a task from its shell; a 'cli' agent's `binary` is that command. None of them on PATH = the agent can lead (it starts the others) but cannot be the lead's subordinate: work waits in its inbox until the owner opens it. `adapter.review_launch` is the command that runs the agent on a review WITHOUT the right to write (`read_only_by`: sandbox, permissions or hook; `verified`: the date and what a write-attempt probe showed). An agent without one cannot hold a read_only role (roles.json): a role does not stop a session with edit rights from editing, the launch does. Adapters are taken from THIS file only: a project agents.json cannot change them.

agents.name: Gemini, via Antigravity CLI

review_launch.requires_settings: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json must allow ONLY mcp(*), read_file(*) and one read-only command rule — no write_file(*), no command(*): headless agy cannot prompt, so every tool or command outside the allow list is auto-denied. The rule used: command(regex:^(git (diff|log|show|status|blame|rev-parse|ls-files|grep)|rg|grep|cat|head|tail|wc|ls)( [^><|;&`$]*)?$) — no redirection, pipes, chaining or substitution. command(*) is NOT read-only: with it agy retries a sandbox-blocked write with the sandbox bypassed and succeeds (seen 2026-10-04). A denial ends the whole headless run, so a reviewer must stay within these commands. Nothing in this launch enforces the settings; whoever changes them breaks the guarantee.

verified.evidence: gemini-3.6-flash-low, inside the project's git tree (a trusted workspace), with the settings above: reading CLAUDE.md and running git log --oneline -1 worked; creating a file with the file-writing tool was auto-denied ('a tool required the write_file permission'); `echo written > FILE`, a retry with the sandbox bypassed, and `git log ... > FILE` were auto-denied ('required the command permission'); no file appeared and git status was unchanged. Control with command(*) allowed: the shell write failed in the sandbox ('operation not permitted') and then succeeded through a sandbox bypass. collab whoami was not reachable in these runs because gemini was not yet in the machine's composition (collab-mcp: no agent "gemini" is registered) — to re-check once it is.

adapter.note: Owner decision 2026-09-15: queue first, launch by hand — nothing here starts a paid agent on its own. Back in the catalog 2026-09-30 (owner): whether it works in the orchestration is the person's composition, chosen in the panel's wizard.
adapter.verified_against: agy 1.2.6, read 2026-09-30 from `agy --help` and `agy mcp --help` (no model call): -p/--print, --model, --effort are as in 1.1.8; `agy mcp list` shows the collab entry the installer writes to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json. First verified live on agy 1.1.8 (2026-09-15): a headless `agy -p` reached collab's whoami. `args` omits --model/--effort, chosen at invocation time like Codex's.
adapter.install_hint: brew install --cask antigravity-cli (or install the Antigravity app, which puts `agy` on PATH), then `agy` once to sign in. Headless calls also need an allow-rule or they auto-deny: add {"permissions":{"allow":["mcp(*)"]}} to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. To review, the allow list must stay read-only — see review_launch.requires_settings (no write_file(*), no command(*)). Then: collab doctor
